Container.Name: HAMAL
Container.Overview: HAMAL is a fast, lightweight, self-hosted file and text sharing server for your local network.[br][br] Send files, photos, documents, and text between computers, phones, and tablets using a web browser. No client installation, cloud storage, or third-party account is required.[br][br] Create a temporary sharing room, then let other devices join instantly by scanning its QR code or opening the room link. Optional PIN protection and automatic room expiration help keep every transfer private and temporary.[br][br] HAMAL runs on your own Unraid server. Your files and shared text stay on your local network and are stored in your configured appdata directory.
Container.Description:
HAMAL is a lightweight, self-hosted file and text sharing server for your local network.
Share files and text between your devices using nothing more than a web browser. No client installation, external cloud storage, or third-party account is required.
FEATURES - File transfers: Send files between devices over your LAN. - Text sharing: Share notes, commands, logs, URLs, and configuration snippets. - QR code pairing: Connect a second device quickly by scanning a room QR code. - Temporary rooms: Transfers are organized into rooms with automatic expiration. - PIN protection: Optionally protect rooms with a PIN. - Self-hosted and private: Your data stays on your own server.
SETUP Open the WebUI after installation. Create a room and connect another device on your local network using the displayed QR code or room link.
DATA HAMAL stores its database, uploaded files, and server secrets in the configured /data directory. Keep the appdata mapping persistent to retain your data across container updates.
Container.Changes: 2026-11-16 - IMPORTANT: Docker data-permission fix. The previously published latest image could recursively change ownership of files under /data in some configurations, including existing Docker Compose or named-volume installations. This did not affect every installation, but it could alter ownership when the container could not write to the data directory as its configured user. The corrected image detects the existing data owner and runs HAMAL without root, preserving existing file ownership instead of recursively changing it. For a brand-new Unraid appdata folder, only the empty folder itself is initialized for Unraid (99:100). Existing databases, uploads, and secrets are not intentionally migrated or recreated. Note: this update does not automatically reverse ownership changes that may already have been made by an earlier image; if your installation has mixed permissions or stops starting after the update, back up your appdata and contact support before changing ownership manually. Existing installations should keep their current appdata mapping and update the container normally; no deletion or data migration is required for a healthy installation. v0.8.14 - Security and reliability release: upload storage limits are now enforced correctly across concurrent uploads, small API requests are size-limited, only the room creator can close a room, PINs are 4-8 digits, participant details stay hidden until the PIN is entered, the upload queue reports errors and keeps going, shared text keeps its exact formatting, and fonts are bundled so pages make no third-party requests. Earlier: Improved the Unraid Apps listing overview with clearer description and paragraph formatting.

Config.Name: Appdata Storage
Config.Description: Persistent storage directory for SQLite database, uploaded files, and server secrets. A new, empty folder is set up automatically for Unraid (99:100). Existing data keeps its owner and is never changed. HAMAL always runs without root privileges.
